getting-started.title: Run SAS programs
getting-started.body:
Run from the folder containing your SAS file, or pass an absolute path. Quote paths containing spaces.

    saslite-custom print_food.sas
    saslite-custom "my program.sas"
    saslite-custom /path/to/project/program.sas
    saslite-custom --version

Execute SAS text directly:

    saslite-custom -e 'data demo; x=42; run; proc print data=demo; run;'

Both saslite-custom and saslite launch this custom build within its installed environment. PATH and active virtual environments determine which installation runs; check --version. See help installation for setup. Each ordinary run starts a fresh session. WORK datasets do not persist between runs.

plots.title: Readable plots in the terminal
plots.body:
TTEST and NPAR1WAY plots print automatically as monospaced text. No browser or image terminal is required. Exact values remain in the statistical tables.

    saslite-custom --plot-width 120 program.sas
    saslite-custom --no-plots program.sas

Width range: 40-160 columns. Default uses LINESIZE (80 by default) and available terminal width; --plot-width overrides it. Tables can be wider than plots.

SAS controls:

    ods graphics off;
    ods graphics on;

TTEST selections: ALL, NONE, SUMMARY, HISTOGRAM, BOX, QQPLOT, PROFILES, AGREEMENT and local INTERVAL. Example: PLOTS=(SUMMARY QQPLOT). SUMMARY includes density histograms, boxes and confidence intervals. Paired designs also support profiles and agreement plots.

NPAR1WAY selections: ALL, NONE, WILCOXONBOXPLOT (WILCOXON), FPBOXPLOT (FP), and local BOXPLOT for raw data. Example: PLOTS=(WILCOXONBOXPLOT FPBOXPLOT). Request the corresponding WILCOXON/FP tests. Default boxes show Wilcoxon ranks or FP placements.

Legends: o outlier/observation, * overlapping observations, M mean; boxes span Q1-Q3 with a median line. Histograms use # bars, . normal density and ~ kernel density. Graphs are text adaptations; density bandwidth/binning and rasterization can differ from SAS ODS. Other procedures do not automatically gain these plots.

python.title: Python API and other project environments
python.body:
Use the Python interpreter from the environment where this custom package is installed:

    python your_script.py

In Python:

    from saslite import SasInterpreter
    sas = SasInterpreter()
    result = sas.execute('data demo; x=42; run;')
    if not result.success:
        raise RuntimeError(result.error)
    print(sas.get_dataset('WORK', 'DEMO'))

sas.execute_file('program.sas') loads script-adjacent configuration. sas.execute(text) uses the current session and does not automatically discover project configuration. Inspect result.success, result.error and result.steps; each step can contain errors, warnings and output_messages. See help installation for installing a release wheel into another environment. The legacy saslite-python launcher is available only in previously configured shared installations.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting and current limits
troubleshooting.body:
Command not found: activate the environment where you installed the package. For pipx or legacy shared installs, check their launcher directory is on PATH. Check --version to confirm the custom build.

Library/dataset not found: verify the .saslite.json beside your script, or pass --lib NAME=/actual/data/folder. The library must point to a directory containing the named dataset. Relative CSV input paths may require launching from the data folder or using an absolute path.

Parse error: check semicolons, spellings and supported options. SASLite is not a complete SAS runtime. Graphics procedures such as SGPLOT, full ODS reporting, remote SAS servers and many specialized procedures are unavailable. TTEST and NPAR1WAY do not implement BY/FREQ/WEIGHT or exact tests; TTEST is currently normal, two-sided analysis. Some other procedures accept more syntax than they fully execute; inspect results carefully.

Native write error: use WORK for temporary data or actual XPT output for persistence. Renaming XPT to .sas7bdat does not create a native dataset.

Missing statistics displayed as a dot with a warning: insufficient data or an undefined denominator may prevent a test. FP needs exactly two groups with at least two observations each.

Output too wide: reduce --plot-width for plots or use a wider terminal. Save the full output (tables/logs currently go to stderr):

    saslite-custom program.sas > results.txt 2>&1
    saslite-custom program.sas 2>&1 | less -S

Exit status is 0 for a successful run and nonzero for an error. Unknown help topics return 2. Optional GUI launchers require Flask/pywebview, which are not installed in the shared command-line environment.

maintenance.title: Keeping this help current
maintenance.body:
Source for this standalone custom project lives in src/saslite. Help is packaged in src/saslite/cli/help_data.json. CLI options and procedure/function inventories are generated from the implementation.

Update affected help topics and examples for each change. Inspect rendered help, run regression tests, then record the review and build:

    python -m saslite help
    python -m unittest discover -s saslite_custom -p 'test_*.py'
    python saslite_custom/check_help.py --record
    python saslite_custom/build_wheel.py

Use an editable development installation before this workflow. The builder checks procedure coverage and source fingerprints against help_review.json. Record only after reviewing help and passing tests; the guard does not establish semantic correctness. Install the tested wheel in the project and any maintained shared environment. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the release checklist.

installation.title: Installation
installation.body:
Install this custom fork from its source checkout (Python 3.10+):

    python -m venv .venv
    . .venv/bin/activate
    python -m pip install .
    saslite-custom --version
    saslite-custom help

On Windows activate with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell. Installation provides saslite-custom and saslite as equivalent commands in that environment. Optional extras: python -m pip install '.[excel]' or '.[gui]'.

For a shared command available outside a project, install a reviewed release wheel with pipx:

    pipx install /path/to/saslite-0.4.1+custom.6-py3-none-any.whl

Existing shared installations at ~/.local/share/saslite-custom/venv can be upgraded with that environment's Python and the exact wheel path. The legacy saslite-python launcher is specific to that installation, not supplied by a normal pip install. Public saslite upgrades can replace custom features. Use an isolated environment and check --version.

UNIVARIATE.title: Univariate summaries
UNIVARIATE.body:
Descriptive distribution summaries for VAR variables. Full SAS NORMAL/PLOT options are not implemented.

    proc univariate data=tmp1.food; var Desir; run;

SORT.title: Sort observations
SORT.body:
BY keys, DESCENDING and NODUPKEY are supported. Use OUT= for a separate result.

    proc sort data=tmp1.food out=sorted; by Couleur Desir; run;

SQL.title: Queries and table operations

IMPORT.title: Import delimited data

EXPORT.title: Export delimited data
EXPORT.body:
DATA=, OUTFILE=, DBMS= and DELIMITER= select output.

    proc export data=tmp1.food outfile="food.csv" dbms=csv; run;

APPEND.title: Append datasets
APPEND.body:
Append DATA to BASE. This modifies BASE; native SAS7BDAT members cannot be overwritten.

    proc append base=combined data=more_rows; run;

DATASETS.title: Manage a library
DATASETS.body:
CONTENTS, DELETE and basic MODIFY/RENAME operations. DELETE removes the named datasets. Use WORK for temporary examples.

    proc datasets library=work; contents; quit;

COPY.title: Copy library members
COPY.body:
IN= and OUT= select libraries; SELECT or EXCLUDE limits the members. Persistent output uses XPT rather than native SAS7BDAT.

    proc copy in=tmp1 out=work; select food; run;

TRANSPOSE.title: Transpose data
TRANSPOSE.body:
DATA=, OUT=, PREFIX=, NAME= and VAR/ID/BY statements are supported.

    proc transpose data=tmp1.food out=transposed; var Desir; run;

COMPARE.title: Compare datasets
COMPARE.body:
BASE= and COMPARE= select datasets. VAR/ID, OUT=, LISTVAR and BRIEF are available.

    proc compare base=original compare=changed; var Desir; run;

FORMAT.title: Define basic display formats
FORMAT.body:
VALUE maps numeric/character keys and ranges to labels. Full SAS catalog behavior is not implemented.

    proc format; value groupfmt 1='First' 2='Second'; run;
